clusters.association: Ending a >1-year IPO freeze mechanically reopens an underwriting revenue channel for listed brokers with strong equity-financing franchises. Fresh quarterly conversion cannot exist immediately, so pre-event business mix/market share and the regulatory quantity change are the core evidence.

FTZ launch changed policy expectations, but many listed 'concept' exposures had unclear company-level monetization while property and concept equities had already repriced sharply. Use as a test that the route does not accept narrative-only policy themes.

Cash crunch and selective liquidity injections directly affect funding conditions, but bank/broker incidence is broad and offsetting; require a uniquely quantified company asymmetry rather than generic beta.

guardrails: No 2014 operating results may be used before freeze.
The IPO-restart route can use pre-event underwriting market share and explicit regulatory issuance quantity, but not later IPO fee revenue.
FTZ concept exposure without mechanical company economics is rejected regardless of price momentum.
No broad market momentum is sufficient by itself.
